overview: China Life Insurance Company Limited is China's largest life insurer by gross written premiums and total assets, offering life, annuity, health and accident insurance to approximately 327-328 million long-term policyholders through the country's largest sales force. Established in 1949 and restructured for its 2003 overseas (H-share, HKEX: 2628) and 2007 domestic (A-share, SSE: 601628) listings, the Company is effectively controlled by the PRC Ministry of Finance via parent China Life Insurance (Group) Company, making it a core state financial institution rather than a purely market-driven enterprise. It operates almost entirely within mainland China, distributing through individual agents, bancassurance, group insurance and online channels, and is simultaneously one of the country's largest institutional investors through its controlling stakes in China Life Asset Management Company and China Life Pension Company.

business_model.summary: China Life earns revenue from underwriting profit (premiums less claims, benefits and expenses) across life, annuity, health and accident lines, plus investment income earned on the large float of assets backing policy reserves (RMB7.4 trillion of investment assets at FY2025). Gross written premiums of RMB729,887 million in FY2025 were split roughly 82% life insurance, 16% health insurance and 2% accident insurance, with life insurance itself skewing toward long-duration participating/endowment and annuity products. Renewal premiums (RMB495,808 million, 68% of GWP) provide a large recurring base layered on top of first-year new business (RMB234,079 million). Under IFRS 17 (adopted FY2023), reported 'insurance revenue' (RMB214,136 million in FY2025) reflects only the service-margin release rather than cash premiums received, so GWP remains the more intuitive top-line KPI. Investment income is highly variable: gross investment income rose from RMB308,251 million in FY2024 to RMB387,694 million in FY2025 (yield 5.50% to 6.09%) and surged again in H1 2026 (RMB314,504 million, yield 5.58% vs 3.29% in H1 2025) on strong Chinese equity markets, materially amplifying earnings swings.

revenue_streams.name: Life insurance (whole life, term, endowment) GWP
Gross investment income (float)
revenue_streams.trend: volatile, highly correlated with A-share/bond markets

business_model.customer_type: B2C mass-market and affluent retail policyholders, plus small/micro enterprises and government-sponsored programs via the group channel
business_model.geographic_mix: Virtually 100% Mainland China; no meaningful international premium base
business_model.distribution_mix: Individual agent channel ~75% of GWP (RMB551,790m FY2025, 587,000-610,000 agents), bancassurance ~15% (RMB110,874m FY2025, growing fastest, +45.5% YoY), group insurance ~4% (RMB26,230m), other/online channels ~6% (RMB40,993m, online premiums RMB114,789m)

competitive_position.market_position: Largest life insurer in China by gross written premiums, total assets and life/health reserves (ranked No.1 globally among life and health insurers by reserve scale per S&P Global Market Intelligence's 'Top 50 Global Life Insurers'); among the top 5-10 Chinese insurers that together generate roughly 95% of industry profit, reflecting an increasingly consolidated, scale-advantaged competitive landscape.

moat_factors.description: Controlled by the PRC Ministry of Finance via China Life Insurance (Group) Company; confers policyholder trust, access to government-sponsored health/pension programs, and an implicit sovereign backstop, at the cost of being steered toward national policy objectives (inclusive insurance, rural revitalisation, 'Five Priorities' of finance) over pure profit maximization.
Largest individual agent force in the industry (587,000-610,000 agents) plus bancassurance relationships with 100+ banks and ~77,000 bank outlets; difficult and slow for competitors to replicate.
One of the first state-approved insurers (1949 predecessor), now carrying a globally recognized brand (Forbes Global 2000, ranked 89th in 2025) that supports persistency and renewal retention.
RMB7.4-7.9 trillion investment portfolio and controlling stakes in China Life AMC and China Life Pension Co. give scale and diversification advantages in asset management that smaller insurers lack.

China's insurance licensing regime (NFRA) limits new entrants, but does not meaningfully constrain existing large competitors (Ping An, CPIC, foreign JVs like AIA) from competing for the same agent and bancassurance pools.

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on an aging, shrinking traditional agent-recruitment model even as the company pushes 'high-quality' agent reform; industry-wide agent headcount has been in multi-year decline

Profitability highly geared to investment markets (A-share equities and long bond yields) rather than pure underwriting discipline, producing earnings volatility unattractive to investors seeking stable compounding
State-directed mandate (inclusive insurance, rural coverage, serving 'national strategies') can crowd out purely commercial capital allocation decisions
Product mix still weighted toward guaranteed-return/participating savings products rather than higher-margin protection business, exposing the balance sheet to spread compression as rates fall
Perceived governance/related-party overhang from extensive connected transactions with parent China Life Group, AMC, Pension Company and CLP&C

growth_drivers: Value of new business (VNB/'value of one year's sales') growth: RMB45,752 million in FY2025, up 35.7% YoY, and RMB38,167 million in H1 2026, up 33.7% YoY, driven by richer product margins (new business margin by first-year premium rose to 35.0% in FY2025 from 25.7% in FY2024) as the Company shifts toward 'semi-priced' (participating) products

Bancassurance channel expansion: GWP up 45.5% YoY in FY2025 and 12.4% YoY in H1 2026, with first-year regular premiums growing even faster, as the Company deepens bank partnerships and improves channel productivity

Shift toward 'semi-priced'/participating insurance business to reduce guaranteed-rate liability costs amid falling interest rates, with participating products reaching ~50% of individual-agent first-year regular premiums in FY2025 (up from a much smaller share) and guaranteed rates on new liabilities declining for three consecutive years

Health, retirement and senior-care ecosystem buildout: 20 residential senior-care projects across 16 cities, health/senior-care platform users above 53 million, third-pillar private pension and commercial annuity products, and new first-of-their-kind health products (disability income, nursing benefits, maternity/infant, senior-specific disease coverage)

Embedded value compounding: EV grew from RMB1,401,146 million (FY2024) to RMB1,467,876 million (FY2025) to RMB1,614,207 million (H1 2026), driven by expected return, strong VNB generation and (in H1 2026) a positive investment experience variance from rising equity markets

Digital/AI transformation ('Digitalised China Life' strategy): AI-assisted underwriting (96.8% intelligent approval rate in H1 2026), claims automation (>75% of claims handled via digital/intelligent channels), and a trusted data space pilot, aimed at structurally lowering unit costs and improving persistency

Industry consolidation tailwind: top 5-10 insurers capturing a rising share of sector profit, favoring scale leaders like China Life as smaller/weaker insurers retrench under tighter bancassurance commission and solvency rules

business.risk: Agent force attrition and productivity pressure
business.description: Industry-wide agent headcount has fallen sharply over the past several years (reported near 2.1 million industry-wide in 2026, down from several times that at the peak) even as China Life's own reported individual-agent count has been comparatively resilient (587,000 at FY2025, ~610,000 at H1 2026); continued reliance on recruitment-driven growth versus productivity-driven growth is a structural question for the channel.

Bancassurance is growing faster than the historically higher-margin individual agent channel; new NFRA rules on 'aligning sales practices with regulatory filings' (effective mid-2026) compress bancassurance commissions industry-wide, which Fitch expects will subdue near-term sector premium growth (H1 2026 industry premium growth of ~3.6% YoY) even as it pushes the industry toward healthier, less commission-dependent growth longer term.

A substantial back book of traditional, fixed-guaranteed-rate policies sold in higher-rate eras continues to run off slowly; while new business is shifting to 'semi-priced' participating products with lower guarantees, the existing liability stock still carries meaningful guaranteed-rate spread risk.

business.risk: Intensifying competition, including from technology/internet platforms
business.description: Management's own FY2025 outlook flags 'cross-sector competition from technology giants and internet platforms... getting increasingly acute' alongside traditional insurer rivalry (Ping An, CPIC, foreign JVs).

financial.description: Comprehensive solvency ratio fell from 207.76% (FY2024) to 174.01% (FY2025), and core solvency ratio fell from 153.34% to 128.77%, driven by interest rate changes and higher equity allocation; still well above the ~100%/50% regulatory minimums but the trend direction bears monitoring, particularly if equity markets reverse or long rates fall further.

Equity financial assets (common stocks, funds, other equity) rose from 19.19% of investment assets at FY2024 to 22.57% at FY2025 and 24.27% at H1 2026, with the Company explicitly 'making decisive increases in equity investments' (open-market equity investments exceeding RMB1.2 trillion, up >RMB450bn YoY); this materially raises earnings and net-asset sensitivity to A-share/H-share market swings, as shown by the 2-3x investment income swings between recent half-years.

Long-duration life/annuity liabilities are matched against a portfolio still ~70% in fixed-maturity instruments plus a growing equity sleeve; reinvestment risk on maturing bonds in a low-rate environment pressures net interest spread over the multi-decade liability horizon.
The Company uses financial assets sold under agreements to repurchase (RMB331,863 million at FY2025, up 119% YoY) for liquidity management, adding a modest funding/rollover risk layer.

regulatory.description: China Life adopted IFRS 17 (Insurance Contracts) and IFRS 9 (Financial Instruments) from 1 January 2023, restating FY2022 comparatives for insurance contracts; this creates a structural break in reported revenue and net income between pre-2023 and post-2023 periods (captured as RevenueRestated/NetIncomeRestated KPIs) and changes how 'insurance revenue' and profit emergence are recognized versus the previously used premium-based presentation.

regulatory.risk: NFRA tightening of sales practices and commission structures
regulatory.description: New rules on 'aligning sales practices with regulatory filings' and a dynamic adjustment mechanism tying guaranteed product rates to market interest rates are being implemented across 2025-2026, directly affecting bancassurance commission economics and new-product pricing flexibility.

As a state-controlled 'systemically important' financial institution, the Company is expected to serve national policy objectives (inclusive insurance, rural revitalisation, support for 'new quality productive forces' and the real economy), which can direct capital or underwriting activity toward non-pure-return objectives.

Fitch and other observers expect tightening reserve/capital requirements combined with rising equity exposure to pressure solvency ratios sector-wide; further regulatory tightening could force capital raises or constrain growth.

macro.description: As one of China's largest institutional investors, the Company holds credit bonds and debt-type financial products concentrated in banking, transportation, non-bank finance, utilities and energy (over 99% AAA-rated per management); while property-direct exposure is not separately broken out in the extracted filings, broader China insurer balance sheets carry indirect exposure to property-sector credit stress through bank and local-government-financing-vehicle-linked holdings.

Chinese government bond yields have trended down for years, compressing reinvestment yields on the ~57% of the portfolio held in bonds and pressuring net interest spread on long-duration guaranteed liabilities; management explicitly cites 'the change in market interest rates' as a driver of both lower solvency ratios and higher insurance contract liabilities.

With equity allocation now above 24% of investment assets, swings in Chinese equity markets flow directly into gross investment income, embedded value movement and net profit, as evidenced by investment income more than tripling in H1 2026 versus H1 2025 on a stock market upswing — a dynamic that can reverse just as sharply in a downturn.

macro.risk: China macro growth slowdown / consumer demand
macro.description: Slower broader economic growth and consumer caution can dampen demand for high-ticket, long-duration savings and protection products sold through the agent and bancassurance channels.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Chinese life insurance industry growth has slowed and is consolidating toward the largest players; Fitch projected ~3.6% YoY premium growth for H1 2026 industry-wide as new bancassurance commission rules took effect, with the top 5-10 insurers (including China Life) capturing roughly 95% of sector profit.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Underwriting/premium growth is only moderately cyclical, but reported earnings are highly cyclical/volatile due to investment income's sensitivity to A-share equity markets and bond yields, which dominate period-to-period profit swings (e.g., FY2025 net profit +44.1% YoY and H1 2026 net profit +228.6% YoY, both driven primarily by investment gains).
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High — falling long-end rates compress reinvestment yields on the fixed-income-heavy portfolio and increase the present value of guaranteed liabilities, while rising rates (all else equal) would relieve spread pressure; the Company has responded by shifting new business toward participating ('semi-priced') products with rates that reset with the market.
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Minimal direct FX exposure — business and investments are overwhelmingly RMB-denominated; the H-share listing (2628.HK) trades in HKD, creating a currency translation/quotation layer between RMB fundamentals and the HKD-quoted share price but not an operational FX risk.
key_input_costs: Long-term interest rates (reinvestment yield on bond portfolio)
Credit spreads on corporate/financial bonds and debt-type financial products
Agent commission and bancassurance commission rates (regulated)

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 net profit attributable to equity holders rose 228.6% YoY to RMB134,489 million on surging investment income (gross investment income +3.14x to RMB314,504m, yield up 229bps to 5.58%); gross written premiums grew a more modest 2.2% to RMB536,634 million and value of half-year's sales rose 33.7% to RMB38,167 million. Interim dividend raised 50.4% YoY to RMB3.58 per 10 shares.
UBS reportedly raised its FY2026 net profit forecast for China Life by 37% following the H1 2026 results, maintaining a Buy rating with a HK$40 price target, citing investment income strength.

Equity allocation within the investment portfolio rose to 24.27% of investment assets (from 22.57% at FY2025-end), with management explicitly stating it is making 'decisive increases in equity investments' and expanding allocation to high-dividend stocks and new-quality-productive-forces sectors.

New NFRA rules on 'aligning sales practices with regulatory filings' took effect for the bancassurance channel, tightening commission structures industry-wide; Fitch expects this to subdue near-term sector premium growth while improving long-run business quality.

Southbound (mainland-to-HK) buying of China Life H-shares surged, reportedly with Ping An Asset Management responsible for roughly 56% of all Southbound holdings in the stock as of late May 2026 — flagged by analysts as a flow dynamic whose sustainability is uncertain.

FY2025 annual results: gross written premiums exceeded RMB700 billion for the first time (RMB729,887 million, +8.7% YoY); net profit attributable to equity holders rose 44.1% YoY to RMB154,078 million; value of one year's sales rose 35.7% to RMB45,752 million; embedded value reached RMB1,467,876 million; comprehensive solvency ratio eased to 174.01% from 207.76%. Final dividend of RMB6.18 per 10 shares proposed, bringing full-year 2025 dividends to RMB8.56 per 10 shares (+31.7% YoY, aggregate payout RMB24,195 million).

Continued build-out of the 'insurance + services' senior-care ecosystem — 20 residential senior-care projects launched across 16 Chinese cities, and healthcare/senior-care platform registrations exceeding 53 million cumulative users by FY2025-end.

guidance.as_of: FY2025 Annual Report (March 2026) and H1 2026 Interim Report (September 2026)

items.target: Sufficient capital to meet 2026 insurance business expenditures and new general investment needs
items.notes: Management states it anticipates sufficient capital for 2026 needs and will arrange financing based on capital market conditions if new strategies require it; no specific quantitative capital target given.

items.target: Continue reducing guaranteed rates on new business and growing the 'semi-priced' (participating) product share
items.notes: Guarantee rates on new business liabilities have declined for three consecutive years; participating products reached ~50% of individual-agent first-year regular premiums in FY2025, management intends to continue this shift under the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030).

items.target: Build a 'world-class life insurance company with Chinese characteristics' under the 15th Five-Year Plan, emphasizing digital/AI transformation, risk management upgrades and new growth engines
items.vs_prior: new multi-year framework (successor to the concluded 14th Five-Year Plan)
items.notes: Qualitative strategic framework rather than numeric targets; no disclosed quantitative revenue, VNB or margin targets for FY2026 specifically in the extracted filings.

guidance.management_commentary: The Chairman's FY2025 statement highlighted record core performance indicators, continued leadership in business scale and value, and the 'solid foundation' built for the 15th Five-Year Plan, while flagging that 'the external environment is complex and volatile' with intensifying competitive dynamics (including from technology/internet platforms) and an industry-wide transition from conventional to new growth drivers. The H1 2026 Interim Report reiterated a comprehensive risk-management framework (five-tier structure, seven risk types) and noted the Company's Class A/AAA integrated risk rating streak (32 consecutive quarters of Class A as of H1 2026). No explicit forward revenue, premium or net-income guidance figures were disclosed in the extracted filings; UBS's post-results FY2026 net profit forecast upgrade (+37%) and HK$40 target are sell-side, not management, guidance.

bull_case: Industry-leading scale (largest GWP, total assets and agent force in China) combined with ongoing sector consolidation that is concentrating profit share among the top players, positioning China Life to keep gaining relative share as smaller insurers retrench

Value of new business and embedded value are both compounding at double-digit rates (VNB +35.7% FY2025, +33.7% H1 2026; EV +4.8% FY2025, +10% H1 2026), evidencing genuine economic value creation beyond headline accounting profit, with EV now above RMB1.6 trillion against a market capitalization that analysts (e.g., Simply Wall St's DCF) argue sits at a steep discount to intrinsic/appraisal value

Shift toward participating/semi-priced products structurally de-risks the balance sheet from guaranteed-rate spread compression as China's long-term rates stay low, improving future earnings quality and solvency resilience

State ownership (Ministry of Finance-controlled) provides implicit credit support, regulatory goodwill and privileged access to government-sponsored health/pension business lines unavailable to private-sector competitors

Equity market upswings (as seen in H1 2026) can produce dramatic earnings beats given the growing equity allocation, offering optionality for shareholders if China's capital markets continue to recover, alongside a rising dividend (FY2025 aggregate payout +31.7% YoY, H1 2026 interim dividend +50.4% YoY)
bear_case: Reported earnings are now heavily investment-market-driven rather than underwriting-driven; the same equity exposure that produced the H1 2026 profit surge (+228.6% YoY) could just as easily reverse sharply in a Chinese equity market downturn, and growing equity allocation (24.27% of investment assets at H1 2026, up from 19.19% a year earlier) raises that sensitivity further

Declining solvency ratios (comprehensive solvency ratio down from 207.76% to 174.01% in FY2025) reflect both lower rates and rising risk-asset allocation; continued regulatory tightening on capital requirements could eventually constrain growth or dividend capacity

Structural headwinds from falling long-term Chinese interest rates continue to pressure reinvestment yields on the ~70% fixed-income portfolio backing long-duration guaranteed liabilities, a multi-decade drag that product-mix shifts can only partially offset

New NFRA rules tightening bancassurance commissions (effective mid-2026) and ongoing agent-sales-system reform create near-term premium growth headwinds (Fitch's ~3.6% industry H1 2026 premium growth estimate) even as they aim to improve long-run quality

As a state-controlled entity, capital allocation and underwriting priorities can be directed toward national policy objectives (inclusive insurance, rural coverage, supporting 'the real economy') rather than purely shareholder-value-maximizing decisions, and governance is complicated by extensive related-party transactions with the parent Group, AMC, Pension Company and CLP&C
